abstract: OpenAI's preprint, whose main theorem states that $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\Re s>7/8$, and Liu's improvements work with residue symbols over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$. One input is a second-moment bound for Möbius-weighted sums of residue symbols, proved through Patterson's cubic theta function. We study the quartic analogue over $\mathbb Q(i)$, where no such theta description is available. For primary squarefree $c$ with split prime factors, the normalised quartic Gauss sum satisfies $\gamma_1(c)^2=\mu(c)\,(c/|c|)\,\chi_c(-1)$, a form of the classical square formula, so it carries the Möbius function in its square. A row twist carries $\mu$ in this way only in one orientation, where the rows are Gauss sums at cube numerators; there the quartic theta residue vanishes on all but the $\asymp X^{1/2}$ rows with squarefull odd part. We prove that the mean square of the carrier sums over rows of norm about $X$ is $\ll X^{2+\theta+\varepsilon}$ whenever twisted quartic Möbius large sieves have excess $B^{\theta}$ uniformly in twists of conductor up to $X^{1/2-2\theta}$ and in coprimality conditions of norm up to $2X$. Without the last restriction the hypothesis is false. The largest shortfall occurs where rows and columns both have norm about $X$, and there the Möbius sieve is the Poisson dual of the carrier energy itself. De Faveri's quartic large sieve gives $X^{9/4+\varepsilon}$, and GRH gives $X^{2+\varepsilon}$; heuristically, for rows and columns of equal norm and with pointwise control of $1/L$, a zero-density estimate with exponent $\kappa$ gives excess $\max(0,1-2/\kappa)$. In a transcription of Liu's optimisation, labelled a model and stated in full, every admissible point has exponent at least $9/10$ for the generic excess $1/4$, and beating Liu's $0.87446830769$ needs $\theta<0.18617$; the model's direct-side assumption fails for the one complete quartic observation known. Up to $X=2^{15}$ the carrier energy is within $6\%$ of the random-phase expectation. No zero-free region is proved.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary: Scope corrections only; Theorem 3.1 and its proof are unchanged. (1) Following the previous review, the abstract and Section 1 now say that the zero-density calculation concerns rows and columns of equal norm and assumes pointwise control of 1/L, not the full hypothesis M4. (2) Section 4 accounts for repeated characters when transferring the density estimate of [7, Cor. 1.5], whose index is fourth-power-free, to the ordinary rows, and does the same for the conductor-ordered estimate of rStation Paper 104 [15]. That estimate lowers the exponent only for sigma > 0.8276, so the excess 0.28430 is unchanged (new supplement script p104_density_compare.py). (3) Section 5 records exponent-level evidence that assumption (T2) fails for the complete quartic observation of rStation Paper 103 [14]: even a perfect carrier energy leaves the trivial bound there. So the threshold 0.18617 describes the model only. References [14], [15] added.
title: Quartic Gauss sums with a Möbius carrier, and the large-sieve input a quartic version of the 7/8 method would need
